name: slices
doc:
slices: generic algorithms over []T (Go's slices + sort).
Sorting is stable (bottom-up merge sort with insertion-sorted runs).
Functions that build a new slice say so; the others work in place.

items.name: All
items.signature: func All<T>(xs []T, f func(T) bool) bool
items.doc: True if every element satisfies f (true for an empty slice).
items.summary: True if every element satisfies f (true for an empty slice).

items.name: BinarySearch
items.signature: func BinarySearch<T: Ordered>(xs []T, x T) (int, bool)
items.doc:
Searches sorted xs for x: the index where x is (or would be inserted)
and whether it is there.
items.summary: Searches sorted xs for x: the index where x is (or would be inserted) and whether it is there.

items.name: BinarySearchFunc
items.signature: func BinarySearchFunc<T, K>(xs []T, target K, cmp func(T, K) int) (int, bool)
items.doc: Like BinarySearch with cmp(element, target) returning <0, 0, >0.
items.summary: Like BinarySearch with cmp(element, target) returning <0, 0, >0.

items.name: Chunk
items.doc:
Consecutive sub-slices of n elements (the last may be shorter). They
share xs's storage. Panics if n < 1.
items.summary: Consecutive sub-slices of n elements (the last may be shorter).

items.name: Clone
items.doc: A copy of xs (nil stays empty).
items.summary: A copy of xs (nil stays empty).

items.name: Compact
items.doc:
New slice with runs of equal consecutive elements replaced by one
(Go's Compact; on a sorted slice this is Unique).
items.summary: New slice with runs of equal consecutive elements replaced by one (Go's Compact; on a sorted slice this is Unique).

items.name: CompactFunc
items.signature: func CompactFunc<T>(xs []T, eq func(T, T) bool) []T
items.doc: Like Compact with an equality function.
items.summary: Like Compact with an equality function.

items.name: Compare
items.doc: Lexicographic comparison: -1, 0 or +1.
items.summary: Lexicographic comparison: -1, 0 or +1.

items.name: Concat
items.doc: Concatenation of two slices (a new slice).
items.summary: Concatenation of two slices (a new slice).

items.name: Contains
items.signature: func Contains<T: Comparable>(xs []T, x T) bool
items.doc: True if x is in xs.
items.summary: True if x is in xs.

items.name: ContainsFunc
items.signature: func ContainsFunc<T>(xs []T, f func(T) bool) bool
items.doc: True if some element satisfies f.
items.summary: True if some element satisfies f.

items.name: Count
items.signature: func Count<T>(xs []T, f func(T) bool) int
items.doc: Number of elements satisfying f.
items.summary: Number of elements satisfying f.

items.name: Delete
items.signature: func Delete<T>(xs []T, i int, j int) []T
items.doc: New slice without the elements xs[i..j].
items.summary: New slice without the elements xs[i..j].

items.name: DeleteFunc
items.doc: New slice without the elements satisfying del.
items.summary: New slice without the elements satisfying del.

items.name: Equal
items.doc: True if a and b have the same length and equal elements.
items.summary: True if a and b have the same length and equal elements.

items.name: EqualFunc
items.signature: func EqualFunc<T, U>(a []T, b []U, eq func(T, U) bool) bool
items.doc: Like Equal with an equality function.
items.summary: Like Equal with an equality function.

items.name: Fill
items.doc: Sets every element of xs to v.
items.summary: Sets every element of xs to v.

items.name: Filter
items.doc: New slice of the elements satisfying keep.
items.summary: New slice of the elements satisfying keep.

examples.name: ExampleFilter
examples.code:
var even = slices.Filter([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], (x int) => x % 2 == 0)
println(even)

items.name: Flatten
items.doc: Concatenation of all the slices.
items.summary: Concatenation of all the slices.

items.name: GroupBy
items.signature: func GroupBy<T, K: Comparable>(xs []T, key func(T) K) []Pair<K, []T>
items.doc: Groups the elements by key, in first-seen key order.
items.summary: Groups the elements by key, in first-seen key order.

items.name: Index
items.signature: func Index<T: Comparable>(xs []T, x T) int
items.doc: Index of the first x in xs, or -1.
items.summary: Index of the first x in xs, or -1.

items.name: IndexFunc
items.signature: func IndexFunc<T>(xs []T, f func(T) bool) int
items.doc: Index of the first element satisfying f, or -1.
items.summary: Index of the first element satisfying f, or -1.

items.name: Insert
items.doc: New slice with vals inserted at index i (0 <= i <= len(xs)).
items.summary: New slice with vals inserted at index i (0 <= i <= len(xs)).

items.name: IsSorted
items.doc: True if xs is sorted ascending.
items.summary: True if xs is sorted ascending.

items.name: IsSortedFunc
items.signature: func IsSortedFunc<T>(xs []T, less func(T, T) bool) bool
items.doc: True if xs is sorted by less.
items.summary: True if xs is sorted by less.

items.name: Map
items.signature: func Map<T, U>(xs []T, f func(T) U) []U
items.doc: New slice of f(x) for every x.
items.summary: New slice of f(x) for every x.

examples.name: ExampleMap
examples.code:
var lens = slices.Map(["go", "zell", "c"], (s string) => len(s))
println(lens)

items.name: Max
items.doc: Largest element; panics on an empty slice.
items.summary: Largest element; panics on an empty slice.

items.name: MaxFunc
items.signature: func MaxFunc<T>(xs []T, less func(T, T) bool) T
items.doc: Largest element by less (the first of equal ones); panics if empty.
items.summary: Largest element by less (the first of equal ones); panics if empty.

items.name: Min
items.doc: Smallest element; panics on an empty slice.
items.summary: Smallest element; panics on an empty slice.

items.name: MinFunc
items.signature: func MinFunc<T>(xs []T, less func(T, T) bool) T
items.doc: Smallest element by less (the first of equal ones); panics if empty.
items.summary: Smallest element by less (the first of equal ones); panics if empty.

items.name: Of
items.doc: New slice of n copies of v.
items.summary: New slice of n copies of v.

items.name: Reduce
items.signature: func Reduce<T, A>(xs []T, init A, f func(A, T) A) A
items.doc: Folds xs from the left: f(...f(f(init, xs[0]), xs[1])..., xs[n-1]).
items.summary: Folds xs from the left: f(...f(f(init, xs[0]), xs[1])..., xs[n-1]).

examples.name: ExampleReduce
examples.code:
var sum = slices.Reduce([1, 2, 3, 4], 0, (acc int, x int) => acc + x)
println(sum)

items.name: Repeat
items.doc: New slice of xs repeated n times. Panics if n < 0.
items.summary: New slice of xs repeated n times.

items.name: Reverse
items.doc: Reverses xs in place.
items.summary: Reverses xs in place.

items.name: Shuffle
items.doc:
Shuffles xs in place (Fisher-Yates); rng(n) must return a random
int in [0, n), e.g. `(n int) => random.IntN(n)`.
items.summary: Shuffles xs in place (Fisher-Yates); rng(n) must return a random int in [0, n), e.g. `(n int) => random.IntN(n)`.

items.name: Sort
items.doc: Sorts xs in place, ascending, stable.
items.summary: Sorts xs in place, ascending, stable.

items.name: SortBy
items.signature: func SortBy<T, K: Ordered>(xs []T, key func(T) K)
items.doc:
Sorts xs in place by key(x), ascending, stable. key is called twice
per comparison; precompute expensive keys.
items.summary: Sorts xs in place by key(x), ascending, stable.

items.name: SortFunc
items.signature: func SortFunc<T>(xs []T, less func(T, T) bool)
items.doc: Sorts xs in place with less (a strict weak order), stable.
items.summary: Sorts xs in place with less (a strict weak order), stable.

examples.name: ExampleSortFunc
examples.code:
var words = ["banana", "kiwi", "apple"]
slices.SortFunc(words, (a string, b string) => len(a) < len(b))
println(words)

items.name: Sum
items.doc: Sum of the elements (zero for an empty slice; concatenation for strings).
items.summary: Sum of the elements (zero for an empty slice; concatenation for strings).

items.name: Unique
items.doc: New slice without duplicates, keeping the first occurrence of each.
items.summary: New slice without duplicates, keeping the first occurrence of each.

items.name: Window
items.doc:
Every window of n consecutive elements, sliding by one (none if
len(xs) < n). They share xs's storage. Panics if n < 1.
items.summary: Every window of n consecutive elements, sliding by one (none if len(xs) < n).

items.name: Zip
items.doc: Pairs of elements at the same index (as long as the shorter slice).
items.summary: Pairs of elements at the same index (as long as the shorter slice).

items.name: Pair
items.doc: A pair of values (the elements of Zip).
items.summary: A pair of values (the elements of Zip).
